question: A and B complete a work in 14 days. If A alone can do it in 63 days, then B alone can do it half of the same work in ______________ days.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by **B** to complete **full work** = (**A × Total**) ÷ (**A − Total**)

⇒ (63 × 14) ÷ (63 − 14) = (63 × 14) ÷ 49 = 18 days.

Time taken for **half of the work** = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (**A + B**) = 14 days

Time taken by **A** alone = 63 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = (Efficiency of **A + B**) − (Efficiency of **A**)

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 9 − 2 = 7 units/day

⇒ **Half of the work** = 126 ÷ 2 = 63 units

⇒ Time taken by **B** for half work = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 days

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Total Work = Time × Efficiency. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the work done, which is usually the ratio of efficiencies if all persons work for the same duration.

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept follows the same logic as Time and Work, where filling is positive work and leakage/emptying is negative work.</p
